8	---
9	
10	# HTTP API
11	
12	Effect HTTP API package for the current TaxKit health endpoint, public
13	calculation endpoints, generated docs and API server route wiring.
14	
15	## Scope
16	
17	`@taxkit/api-http` owns the current HTTP API contract, generated OpenAPI
18	metadata, health and public calculation routes, HTTP status envelopes, thin
19	handler adapters and an in-process test client used by TaxKit apps. Reusable
20	calculator schemas, catalog entries, metadata projections, graph construction,
21	calculation dispatch and schema-guided expected error shaping live in
22	`@taxkit/calculators`.
23	
24	The root export includes `HealthResponse`, the same Schema used by the health
25	endpoint. The API app's smoke check uses this owner to validate the real health
26	response without copying its shape. This addition preserves the health wire
27	format and all existing routes.
28	
29	The implemented API surface is:
30	
31	- `GET /api/health`
32	- `GET /api/docs`
33	- `GET /api/docs/openapi.json`
34	- `GET /api/v1/jurisdictions`
35	- `GET /api/v1/tax-years`
36	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`
37	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId`
38	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema`
39	- `POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`
40	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph`
41	- `GET /api/v1/facts`
42	- `GET /api/v1/rules`
43	- `GET /api/v1/docs/navigation`
44	- `GET /api/v1/docs/page?path=/start/quickstart`
45	- `GET /api/v1/docs/search?term=Quickstart`
46	- `GET /api/v1/docs/markdown?path=/start/quickstart`
47	
48	The public calculation API routes use the reusable calculator catalogue,
49	fact and rule descriptors and graph diagnostics from `@taxkit/calculators`.
50	Every handler, including Calculate, calls `PublicCalculatorService` directly.
51	The HTTP Calculate route supplies its checked route ID, body and query to the
52	same named `calculate` operation used by native RPC. Expected service failures
53	keep the existing HTTP envelope. The status declarations below describe the
54	additional request and operation protections.
55	The SDK is a test-only comparison dependency, rather than a server dependency.
56	
57	`@taxkit/api-http/server` exports `TaxKitApiRoutesLayer` for application-owned
58	service and CORS composition. It also retains `TaxKitServerLayer` with the
59	existing calculator engine and CORS defaults for Bun and in-process consumers.
60	Both server Layers require the caller's `ContentService`. API hosts supply the
61	accepted build output; the HTTP package imports only the compiled content
62	contracts. The native API host supplies its shared calculator service to HTTP
63	and RPC.
64	
65	The `content` group delegates navigation, page lookup and search to that same
66	content service. Markdown returns the owning processed page body as
67	`text/markdown`. Page queries use checked, bounded public addresses; search
68	terms have the owning 100-character limit. Missing pages return fixed typed
69	JSON 404 guidance and a search-source failure returns fixed typed JSON 503
70	guidance, without reflecting paths or source-error messages. Native invalid
71	query responses are empty 400 replies. This surface returns accepted public
72	documentation only, not personal calculation reports.
73	
74	Callers use Effect's generated client directly:
75	`HttpApiClient.make(TaxKitApi, { baseUrl })` from `effect/http-api`, with
76	`TaxKitApi` from `@taxkit/api-http/api` and the caller's `HttpClient`.
77	`TaxKitApiInProcessLive` (`@taxkit/api-http/in-process`) is an in-process
78	`HttpClient` over the same routes for tests and examples. It requires supplied
79	content, runs in the caller's Layer scope and closes each request's scope. The
80	generated client checks the same response Schemas as remote consumers.
81	
82	```ts
83	HTTP calculate
84	
85	API host
86	  -> TaxKitApiRoutesLayer
87	    -> CalculatorApiHandlerLive
88	      -> PublicCalculatorService.calculate({ calculatorId, payload, ...query })
89	        -> selected calculator input decode and CalculationEngine
90	        -> CalculatorRunResponseData
91	      -> existing CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope on expected failure
92	```
93	
94	```ts
95	Tests: in-process HTTP client
96	
97	HTTP API tests
98	  -> HttpApiClient.make(TaxKitApi) over TaxKitApiInProcessLive
99	    -> CalculatorApiHandlerLive
100	      -> PublicCalculatorServiceLive
101	        -> CalculationEngineLive
102	  -> success response equals SDK full-run response
103	  -> CalculatorInputDecodeError maps to CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope
104	```
105	
106	The calculate route imports reusable `CalculatorRun*` schemas and
107	`CalculatorServiceError` from `@taxkit/calculators`. `CalculatorRunRequest`
108	has a `facts` field that is a union of canonical rule-owned input schemas, so
109	generated OpenAPI exposes concrete supported fact shapes under `facts.anyOf`
110	instead of `Schema.Unknown`. HTTP-only names such as
111	`CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope` stay in this package because they describe
112	calculator API transport status encoding. HTTP
113	handlers must not try to select or transform calculator facts locally;
114	`PublicCalculatorService` performs the selected-calculator `inputSchema` decode
115	and returns `CalculatorInputDecodeError` with descriptor-backed help for
116	incompatible calculator/facts combinations.
117	
118	## Main Areas
119	
120	- `src/api.ts`: `TaxKitApi` definition and OpenAPI annotations.
121	- `src/groups/health.ts`: health endpoint schema and route group.
122	- `src/groups/calculators.ts`: public calculation HTTP route schemas, bad
123	  request envelope, OpenAPI annotations and compatibility exports from
124	  `@taxkit/calculators`.
125	- `src/openapi.ts`: package-owned OpenAPI generation, structured
126	  normalization and snapshot formatting for compatibility checks.
127	- `src/handlers/`: server-side thin handler adapters and handler layers.
128	- `src/server/live.layer.ts`: server route layer, CORS middleware, Scalar docs
129	  route, OpenAPI JSON route using the package-owned OpenAPI source and
130	  calculator service layer composition.
131	- `src/server.ts`: server export boundary for `TaxKitServerLayer`.
132	- `src/config.ts`: package-owned client config schema and neutral `httpApi`
133	  config source.
134	- `src/in-process.layer.ts`: in-process `HttpClient` over the routes, for
135	  tests and examples.
136	- `src/response-policy.ts`: the single public cache decision for replies.
137	
138	Export paths:
139	
140	- `@taxkit/api-http`

159	## Runtime Shape

161	The package is built as ESM TypeScript. Runtime exports are split by boundary:
162	
163	- browser-safe consumers use `@taxkit/api-http/api` with Effect's
164	  `HttpApiClient`
165	- server runtimes may use `@taxkit/api-http/server`

168	- handler exports are server-side and should not be imported from browser code
169	
170	`ApiRoutesLive` owns reusable route middleware such as CORS inside this package.
171	App packages should provide a platform HTTP server and process config, not
172	duplicate API route middleware.
173	
174	`@taxkit/api-http/config` owns the reusable client config schema, type and
175	keyed config fragment. Apps should compose that fragment into runtime-specific
176	config modules, then provide server or client environment values through Effect
177	`ConfigProvider` composition. The package owns its env namespaces, including
178	`TAXKIT_API_*` and `VITE_TAXKIT_API_*`. See
179	`docs/architecture/configuration.md`.

181	Current responses are schema-backed with Effect Schema. Calculator response
182	schemas are imported from `@taxkit/calculators`; route-only HTTP envelopes and
183	status annotations stay in this package. The health response is:

330	## Guardrails
331	
332	- Keep browser consumers on `api` with the generated client; do not import server handlers into
333	  browser code.

341	  catalog-driven, scenario-schema decoded and `CalculationEngine` based run.
342	- Keep metadata responses derived from canonical fact descriptors, rule
343	  descriptors, source refs, parameter periods and graph diagnostics from the
344	  owning engine and rule packages.
345	- Keep handlers thin. They may extract route input and translate tagged
346	  service errors to HTTP status envelopes; reusable calculator lookup,

362	## Contract verification boundaries
363	
364	The OpenAPI snapshot test uses Effect FileSystem and the owning JSON Schema
365	codec; the committed normalized snapshot remains the wire-contract oracle.
366	The secret-negative HTTP test encodes its error with CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope.
367	Both test files are checked by `tsconfig.test.json` in `check-types`, including
368	canonical branded identities and explicit Match narrowing of report/error unions.
369	
370	The in-process Fetch adapter retains its required Promise return signature in
371	one exact lint admission. It contains no async orchestration or Effect runner.
372	Real CLI fixtures prove adjacent files reject the signature and the admitted
373	file still rejects async/await. This preserves the current host bridge pending
374	the separate native app composition task; it is not native Worker lifetime proof.
375	
376	The [shared work policy](../../../packages/calculators/README.md#shared-calculation-work-limits) gives the API instance one eight-calculation pool
377	across HTTP and RPC, including individual batch messages, with a five-second
378	operation budget for all nine service methods. Checked capacity and operation-timeout errors become HTTP
379	503/504 envelopes or canonical RPC errors. Website guidance requests
380	manual retry only. This is separate from the body-read and ten-second client
381	budgets. Metadata does not use a calculation place. Native built proof covers a
382	seven-calculation RPC batch plus one HTTP calculation, rejected extra HTTP/SSR/
383	browser calls, HTTP 504/RPC timeouts and reached cleanup. Synchronous CPU work
384	cannot be stopped by a JavaScript timer; a late-result check rejects it after
385	control returns. The native rate policy below is implemented separately; MCP and whole T004
386	qualification remain unfinished.
387	
388	
389	## Shared request admission
390	
391	`@taxkit/api-http/request-boundary` owns the streamed 64 KiB POST body limit and
392	five-second total read deadline. It counts encoded bytes before parsing, closes
393	rejected/interrupted readers and rejects late synchronous reads after control
394	returns. The retained standalone server applies it before calculator decoding;
395	native API and Website hosts use the same owner. The RPC entrypoint re-exports
396	its original four symbols for compatibility. Only the native API host's outer
397	composition covers both HTTP and RPC; a custom route host must supply its own
398	admission middleware.
399	
400	Fixed Schema-owned request errors use HTTP 413 (`request-too-large`, reduce the
401	request) and 408 (`request-timeout`, retry manually). JSON responses use the
402	`error` envelope. Website form hosts select the checked HTML policy, producing a
403	fixed message and link back to the calculators without reflecting input or URLs.
404	The calculation endpoint declares both statuses in OpenAPI. Every metadata
405	endpoint declares 504 for the shared operation timeout; lookup failures retain
406	400. Metadata never consumes a calculation place. No automatic retry is added.
407	
408	
409	Calculator-owned context, help and filter fields use `Option<Option<A>>` in
410	checked TypeScript values: `None` means a missing key, `Some(None)` means a
411	present undefined key, and `Some(Some(value))` means a present value. Owning
412	constructors default omitted keys to `None`. JSON and HTTP query fields retain
413	their ordinary optional representation. Flatten the two absent forms only where
414	they mean the same thing; do not invent a jurisdiction or tax year.
415	
416	Typed client calls use canonical constructor values. Raw HTTP JSON and query
417	strings still encode and decode through the owning request codecs; the OpenAPI
418	snapshot remains the representation contract.
419	
420	
421	The reusable Core calculation error now has a nested Option cause in checked
422	TypeScript values. Its existing HTTP representation is retained, including
423	missing/undefined/null diagnostic forms. This is an absence-owner change, not
424	a diagnostic sanitiser; do not export legacy diagnostic values to telemetry.
425	
426	
427	## Native calculation rate admission
428	
429	The [calculator-owned rate contract](../../calculators/README.md#native-calculation-rate-admission) adds canonical rate/unavailable errors to calculation responses. The native API maps them to HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 60` and fixed 503 guidance, using the existing error envelope. Metadata consumes no rate unit. Owning group Schemas drive generated clients and the OpenAPI snapshot; the standalone Bun host keeps its existing policy.
430	
431	The public page-address refinement and fixed documentation errors now belong
432	to `@taxkit/content`, shared with native documentation RPC. This package retains
433	its existing error exports and HTTP status/media rules. Generated OpenAPI names
434	the same canonical address bound for both the request and returned page.

21	- `./group`: the nine calculator procedures, `TaxKitRpcGroup` and the combined
22	  `TaxKitPublicRpcGroup` used by the server.
23	- `./schemas`: calculator-owned request/result/catalogue/query and content-owned navigation/path
24	  Schemas, checked API origin, contract version and ten-second deadline.

27	- `./service`: closed named client matching the existing calculator service.
28	- `./server`: native POST `/rpc` Layer with JSON serialisation and checked ingress;
29	  requires supplied `PublicCalculatorService` and `ContentService`.
30	- `./live`: configured protocol Layer with a native client scope per named operation;
31	  the app supplies its HttpClient.
32	- `./test`: explicit test-only in-process client over the same handler.
33	- `./testing/fixtures`: deterministic real-calculator and failure fixtures only.
34	- `./request-boundary`: shared native POST body limit, 64 KiB and five seconds.
35	- `./host-telemetry`: API/Website log and reporter containment with fixed fields.

37	Workspace source conditions resolve `src`; ordinary imports and declarations

41	## Failure and lifetime ownership
42	
43	The handler projects calculator errors to a fixed reason without reflecting
44	private issue paths, causes or messages. Contract version disagreement has its
45	own checked error. The server uses the native JSON parser/encoder and validates
46	its unknown request envelopes before native dispatch. Only bounded request IDs,
47	the declared procedure, a bounded batch and correctly shaped headers pass.
48	Malformed JSON/envelopes use the native global defect path; decoded procedure
49	payload failures use the procedure defect encoder.
50	A supported codec hook replaces that path's encoding with a fixed safe value;
51	the procedure also declares a safe defect Schema. No message framing is invented.
52	
53	The private reply codec marks only failures decoding any declared native operation exit.
54	Bad JSON and invalid result shapes become `CalculatorRpcInvalidResponse`.
55	An unrelated adapter defect retains its identity; defects remain defects.
56	The native exit/defect Schema identities and these paths are qualified on
57	Effect 4.0.0, whose RPC APIs remain marked unstable. Requalify on upgrades.
58	
59	A single ten-second budget includes headers and complete body decoding. Earlier
60	caller interruption releases pending body work. Client resources belong to the
61	operation scope; the protocol configuration belongs to the caller Layer.
62	This package creates no runtime or Layer during any operation. A native Worker
63	can suspend between requests, so a receive loop acquired by an earlier request
64	must not be retained for later calls. Public calls omit credentials and reject
65	redirects. The native HTTP transform sets exactly `/rpc`, avoiding the default
66	empty-path client's `/rpc/` redirect. RPC and HTTP tracing are both disabled for
67	this transport; the tests check actual native request headers. The Website's
68	saved local pair test also checks real browser enforcement and CORS.

78	Markdown negotiation, share images and old-app retirement remain unfinished. Re-exported content

225	content/application owner. The client checks that the returned file address
226	matches the requested one. The documentation procedure defect is a fixed literal; the native
227	global fatal path retains its already qualified fixed literal. Internal source
228	diagnostics and raw Causes are not response values. The native API supplies the
229	same generated catalogue for HTTP and RPC. This package imports only compiled
230	content contracts, with no MDX compiler or source collection dependency.
231	
232	Focused documentation tests cover all five calls, valid and incompatible
233	versions, safe expected/global/procedure failures, damaged replies, unrelated
234	adapter defects, exact/oversized encoded byte limits, headers/body deadlines,
235	earlier cancellation, scope close and transport policy. The actual native pair
236	check compares all accepted page values and exact Markdown through these
237	clients across separate Worker requests. Those checks qualify the API/client
238	connection. The Website now composes page/navigation calls over its native
239	binding and checks compiled presentation. Its search interaction uses the same
240	checked catalogue; the Website README and current native journey own the
241	completed search and reader proof.

9	
10	# API and SDK
11	
12	The active T008 candidate adds minimal analytics only in the native API app.
13	The Website supplies fresh browser or original HTML preferences through the
14	shared private header boundary. Its checked flag carries allow/deny without browser identity and
15	cannot bypass normal calculator admission. One app decorator collects catalogue
16	ID/name after success. Pure calculators and SDK package calls remain free of
17	analytics. The [API README](../../apps/api/README.md#analytics-candidate) owns
18	the current bounded collector, background delivery design and remaining proof.
19	
20	TaxKit should publish a reusable API app server and TypeScript SDK around the
21	open-source calculation engine.
22	
23	The API and SDK are part of this repository because they expose reusable tax
24	calculation capabilities through stable, documented boundaries.
25	
26	## Current API runtime
27	
28	See [TypeScript SDK and publishing](../product-specs/typescript-sdk-and-publishing.md)
29	and [SDK public naming and export contract](../product-specs/sdk-public-naming-and-export-contract.md)
30	for the SDK facade, plain TypeScript entrypoint, Effect entrypoint and export
31	contract specs.
32	
33	`apps/api` is the current API runtime owner. It is a standalone Bun process
34	that owns host/port config, process startup through
35	`@effect/platform-bun/BunRuntime.runMain`, Bun request serving and graceful
36	shutdown through Effect interruption and scoped layer finalizers. It delegates
37	API contracts, handlers, schemas and generated docs to `packages/api/http`.
38	
39	API settings use the caller's native ConfigProvider and owning port/host
40	Schemas. Missing ports use `PORT` and then 4000; an invalid present `API_PORT`
41	fails with a bounded settings error. Hosts retain trimming and blank fallback.
42	The app's smoke command has named native HTTP operations, the public
43	`HealthResponse` Schema and existing calculator Schemas. Request deadlines
44	include headers and body decoding (health 15 seconds including retries, other
45	routes five seconds). It checks the OpenAPI calculate path and then runs a
46	plain JavaScript consumer outside the checkout. That command has a 30-second
47	limit, scoped lifetime, checked route evidence and bounded output/error
48	reporting. Failed cleanup remains a failure, including alongside failed work.
49	These checks establish local app/consumer behaviour only.
50	
51	The current implemented API surface is:
52	
53	```txt
54	GET /api/health
55	GET /api/docs
56	GET /api/docs/openapi.json
57	GET /api/v1/jurisdictions
58	GET /api/v1/tax-years
59	GET /api/v1/calculators
60	GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId
61	GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema
62	POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate
63	GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph
64	GET /api/v1/facts
65	GET /api/v1/rules
66	GET /api/v1/docs/navigation
67	GET /api/v1/docs/page?path=/start/quickstart
68	GET /api/v1/docs/search?term=Quickstart
69	GET /api/v1/docs/markdown?path=/start/quickstart
70	```
71	
72	`apps/web` consumes the separate API through native RPC. It must not mount the canonical API or
73	import server-only `@taxkit/api-http` exports.
74	
75	API process entrypoints should be Effect programs run with
76	`@effect/platform-bun/BunRuntime.runMain(...)`. The app owns process config,
77	platform server creation and root lifecycle. The HTTP API package owns
78	`HttpApi` definitions, `HttpApiBuilder.group(...)` handlers, generated docs
79	and reusable route layers. Apps should provide a platform `HttpServer` and
80	serve the package route layer. Packages must not call `Bun.serve`, read
81	process env or own process signal handling.
82	
83	## Current API package
84	
85	The current API package lives under:
86	
87	```txt
88	packages/api/http
89	```
90	
91	Package name:
92	
93	```txt
94	@taxkit/api-http
95	```
96	
97	It owns the current Effect HTTP API definitions, health endpoint schema,
98	server route layer, OpenAPI metadata, typed client helpers and reusable client
99	config schema.
100	
101	`@taxkit/api-http` owns transport contracts, HTTP status annotations, OpenAPI
102	generation, typed HTTP clients, server route layers and thin handler adapters.
103	Reusable calculator catalog entries, metadata transformations, graph assembly
104	and schema-error shaping live in `@taxkit/calculators`. The calculate route
105	calls the supplied `PublicCalculatorService` directly and maps its checked
106	result to the HTTP response. SDK parity is proved by the package tests and
107	packed-consumer checks; the production HTTP handler does not execute through
108	the SDK.
109	
110	`@taxkit/api-http/config` exports the package-owned HTTP API client config
111	schema, type and keyed config fragment. Apps compose that fragment into their
112	own runtime config modules and provide runtime-specific values, such as server
113	process env or Vite client env, through `ConfigProvider` composition instead of
114	redefining API client config keys or env prefixes locally.
115	
116	Runtime app modules should keep app-owned schemas in colocated `schemas.ts`
117	files and derive exported types from those schemas. Server startup files should
118	consume canonical schema values and compose config, layers and runtime lifecycle
119	only.
120	
121	Every public HTTP request and response schema should live in the owning API
122	group or an owning package schema module. If downstream code needs the type,
123	export it from the same module as a schema-derived type. Do not hand-write DTO
124	interfaces or duplicate response shapes in handlers, clients or apps.
125	
126	The public documentation group uses canonical `@taxkit/content` page,
127	navigation and search Schemas. Its thin handlers call `ContentService` and
128	return the same processed page body for Markdown. Both API hosts inject a
129	checked build-time JSON catalogue, without importing the MDX compiler into
130	requests. Page queries are bounded public addresses; search terms and result
131	sizes retain the content owner's limits. Missing-page and source-search
132	failures have fixed typed 404/503 replies; native invalid queries return empty
133	400 replies. These routes contain public documentation, never personal reports.
134	The HTTP server Layers and native in-process client require supplied content.
135	The latter runs native request Effects in caller-owned scopes and does not
136	create an additional web-handler runner.
137	
138	Route-only HTTP envelopes, query schemas and status annotations stay in
139	`@taxkit/api-http`. HTTP-facing names such as
140	`CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope` stay in the transport package because they
141	describe calculator API status encoding. Rule-owned calculator IDs and
142	supported context literals are composed by `@taxkit/calculators`; reusable
143	help modes, calculator run payloads and calculator service errors live in
144	`@taxkit/calculators`.
145	
146	The final calculate-route production graph is:
147	
148	```ts
149	Production: HTTP calculate
150	
151	API host (retained Bun or native Worker candidate)
152	  -> TaxKitApiRoutesLayer
153	    -> CalculatorApiHandlerLive
154	      -> PublicCalculatorService.calculate({ calculatorId, payload, ...query })
155	        -> selected CalculatorCatalogEntry.inputSchema decode
156	        -> constructor-closed typed scenario continuation
157	        -> CalculationEngine and owning rule/scenario Layers
158	        -> CalculatorRunResponseData
159	      -> existing CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope on expected service failure
160	```
161	
162	Metadata routes stay direct service adapters until a broader SDK catalog
163	facade exists:
164	
165	```ts
166	Production: metadata routes
167	
168	CalculatorApiHandlerLive
169	  -> PublicCalculatorService.listCalculators / getCalculator / getCalculatorGraph
170	  -> calculator-owned metadata response schemas
171	  -> CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope for expected lookup/context failures
172	```
173	
174	The SDK Effect full-run graph is:
175	
176	```ts
177	Production: SDK Effect full run
178	
179	Effect consumer
180	  -> @taxkit/sdk/effect calculateRunRequest(descriptor, request)
181	    -> PublicCalculatorService.calculate({ calculatorId, ...request })
182	      -> CalculatorRunServiceRequest
183	      -> CalculatorRunResponse
184	    -> descriptor.decodeOutput(response.report)
185	    -> response with report narrowed to OutputSchema["Type"]
186	
187	Report-only helpers
188	  -> calculateReportRequest(...)
189	    -> calculateRunRequest(...)
190	    -> response.report
191	  -> calculateReport(...)
192	    -> calculateReportRequest(...)
193	```
194	
195	The matching test graph is:
196	
197	```ts
198	Tests: HTTP compared with SDK
199	
200	HTTP API tests
201	  -> TaxKitApiInProcessClientLive
202	    -> CalculatorApiHandlerLive
203	      -> PublicCalculatorServiceLive
204	        -> CalculationEngineLive
205	  -> success response equals SDK full-run response
206	  -> CalculatorInputDecodeError maps to CalculatorApiErrorEnvelope
207	```
208	
209	## Current calculator package
210	
211	The reusable calculator orchestration package lives under:
212	
213	```txt
214	packages/calculators
215	```
216	
217	Package name:
218	
219	```txt
220	@taxkit/calculators
221	```
222	
223	It owns:
224	
225	- reusable calculator catalog schemas and service methods that compose
226	  rule-owned calculator id and context schemas
227	- catalog entries that compose canonical fact descriptors, rule descriptors,
228	  report schemas, scenario layers and rule-pack layers
229	- metadata transformations for calculator, fact, rule and graph responses
230	- schema-guided expected error shaping with descriptor-backed help
231	- calculation execution through `CalculationEngine`
232	- canonical reusable calculator execution schemas named `CalculatorRun*`
233	- canonical reusable calculator failure union named `CalculatorServiceError`
234	- typed propagation of expected domain failures such as `CalculationError`
235	
236	HTTP, SDK, CLI and in-process callers should consume this service instead of
237	implementing calculator business logic locally.
238	
239	## HTTP API package topology
240	
241	The implemented HTTP API package lives at `packages/api/http` and is named
242	`@taxkit/api-http`. It owns Effect HTTP API definitions, calculation endpoint
243	schemas, thin server handlers that delegate to `@taxkit/calculators`, OpenAPI
244	generation, HTTP status annotations and generated HTTP client helpers.
245	
246	## API app scope
247	
248	The reusable API app server lives under:
249	
250	```txt
251	apps/api
252	```
253	
254	It is a reusable server for open-source and integration use. Applications may
255	run their own API servers that import TaxKit packages or call this API, but
256	the app remains a thin transport over the calculation engine.
257	
258	## Endpoint shape
259	
260	Calculation endpoints are calculator, fact, rule and graph oriented rather
261	than jurisdiction-route oriented. Jurisdiction, tax year, rule-pack options and
262	capability filters are request context and metadata, not top-level route
263	families.
264	
265	The public calculation API uses stable generic resources:
266	
267	```txt
268	GET  /api/v1/jurisdictions
269	GET  /api/v1/tax-years
270	GET  /api/v1/calculators
271	GET  /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId
272	GET  /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema
273	POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate
274	GET  /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph
275	GET  /api/v1/facts
276	GET  /api/v1/rules
277	```
278	
279	Calculator IDs may include jurisdiction segments, such as
280	`au.pay.take-home`, but route structure must remain portable to future
281	jurisdictions. Do not add `/api/v1/au/*` as the primary public route shape.
282	
283	Inputs and outputs must decode through Effect Schema. Schema decode failures
284	should return structured issue details, missing/invalid field paths and
285	descriptor-backed help so clients can guide users toward the facts required by
286	the selected calculator. Outputs should include reports, traces, ledgers and
287	diagnostics where relevant.
288	
289	Calculator input-error egress preserves the public tagged shape, normalized
290	field paths and descriptor help, but replaces formatter text that can include
291	the rejected actual value with stable safe text. HTTP, Effect SDK and direct
292	calculator consumers must not receive secrets or machine-local paths copied
293	from invalid inputs.
294	
295	The generic calculate route exposes request facts as a union of canonical
296	rule-owned calculator input schemas, not `Schema.Unknown`. OpenAPI should show
297	the supported fact shapes under `facts.anyOf`; current public shapes include
298	take-home/pay-withholdings input facts and annual-tax input facts. Because
299	Effect HTTP route schemas are not dependent on the `calculatorId` path
300	parameter, `@taxkit/calculators` must decode `payload.facts` again with the
301	selected catalog entry's canonical `inputSchema` before execution. A payload
302	that is valid for a different calculator must fail as
303	`CalculatorInputDecodeError` with descriptor-backed help for the selected
304	calculator.
305	
306	The Effect `4.0.0-rc.117` upgrade changes generated OpenAPI component names
307	to encoded-side names ending in `Encoded` and adds a nested union around
308	supported tax years. The API package owns this document change and its
309	snapshot. Public route paths, status codes and JSON field names remain stable;
310	route tests and the standalone API smoke check cover those runtime claims.
311	
312	Public JSON examples must use canonical schema values, including tagged values
313	such as `GrossPay` and `Money` where the owning schema requires those tags.
314	
315	Calculation/domain failures that are part of the engine contract should remain
316	typed failures and be encoded through the public error envelope. They should
317	not be converted into Effect defects.
318	
319	Metadata and calculation routes may accept a `help` query parameter for richer
320	client guidance. Help output should be generated from canonical schemas, fact
321	descriptors, rule descriptors, graph diagnostics and source references instead
322	of hand-written route-specific DTOs.
323	
324	## Native API Worker candidate
325	
326	The active DEV-74 change adds `apps/api/src/worker.ts`, a native Alchemy
327	Worker class and `.make` entry. Its instance initialisation constructs one
328	router and acquires one calculator service for both `TaxKitApiRoutesLayer`
329	and `TaxKitRpcHttpLayer`. `HttpRouter.toHttpEffect` returns the incoming
330	request Effect; it does not create a backend ManagedRuntime.
331	
332	The host leaves resource addresses deferred during native planning and
333	decodes/caches their bound values through Config on first incoming use.
334	Absent or invalid origins return an empty 503; no address is invented. Native
335	`Worker.URL` supplies its own address; infrastructure composition must supply
336	the matching website Output before the app graph is accepted. Native CORS
337	uses its supported origin predicate: the selected version's single-element
338	array form emits a fixed allow-origin value even for unrelated origins.
339	The predicate omits that header for an unrelated request. Only `content-type`
340	is allowed for the current JSON client, with credentials disabled.
341	
342	POST bodies are read through the native Effect stream with a 64-KiB limit
343	and a total five-second read deadline, before native JSON decoding. Oversized
344	and stalled requests return checked JSON 413/408 guidance with the same CORS policy.
345	The selected native web-request reader does not use `MaxBodySize`, so merely
346	providing that reference would not enforce this limit. Native request
347	conversion retains headers, method, path and remote address.
348	
349	The root installs a closed logger and error reporter before router construction
350	and incoming dispatch. Console egress contains a fixed event, time and severity;
351	raw native messages, Causes and arbitrary annotations do not escape this
352	adapter. Full native trace/export proof remains pending. The native Worker
353	candidate does not establish deployed availability. The T003 acceptance review
354	qualifies the complete local connection; T009 retains safe native trace exports.
355	The retained Bun entry and public HTTP/OpenAPI contract remain available.
356	
357	## TypeScript SDK facade
358	
359	The current private SDK package lives under:
360	
361	```txt
362	packages/sdk/typescript
363	```
364	
365	Current package name:
366	
367	```txt
368	@taxkit/sdk
369	```
370	
371	Preferred public package name at release time:
372	
373	```txt
374	taxkit
375	```
376	
377	If the unscoped package name is unavailable at first publish, continue with
378	`@taxkit/sdk` and keep the same export contract.
379	
380	It owns:
381	
382	- direct in-process calculation facade
383	- plain TypeScript `TaxKit.createClient(...)` client factory and
384	  `TaxKit.{method}` generic helpers
385	- Effect-native `./effect` entrypoint
386	- jurisdiction-specific opt-in subpaths such as `./au`
387	- Layer-backed typed modules that preserve compile-time calculation, fact, rule and period capabilities
388	- typed declarations, provider Layers and bindings shared by plain and Effect entrypoints
389	- exported input and output schemas
390	- typed calculator request builders
391	- examples for Node and browser usage
392	
393	The SDK must not import `@taxkit/api-http`, server handlers or Node-only
394	modules from browser-safe entrypoints. It also must not expose Effect runtime
395	types from the plain TypeScript entrypoint. HTTP clients and OpenAPI transport
396	helpers stay in `@taxkit/api-http`. The SDK is a test-only comparison
397	dependency of the HTTP package; the production HTTP adapter calls the owning
398	calculator service directly.
399	
400	The plain facade maps typed calculator failures, output Schema failures and
401	unexpected defects into stable SDK-owned messages. It preserves a typed
402	`CalculatorServiceError` detail when present, but never projects raw
403	`Cause.pretty` text, rejected values or private paths into either safe results
404	or rejected Promises. Effect consumers continue to receive the typed error
405	channel directly.
406	
407	Plain clients have caller-owned lifetimes. `createClient` creates one private,
408	lazy ManagedRuntime per client, and `dispose(): Promise<void>` interrupts pending
409	work/startup and awaits finalisation. An Effect Ref marks the client closed;
410	an Effect Deferred shares cleanup completion with repeated or overlapping
411	calls. Closing one client does not close another. Closed calculation calls have
412	checked `TaxKitClientDisposedError` detail; cleanup defects produce the safe
413	`TaxKitClientDisposeError`. The private `client.runtime.ts` is the exact Promise
414	and execution host. Actual work is interruptible inside its client scope; public
415	outcome conversion is protected so raw interruption errors do not escape.
416	
417	One-shot generic and AU helpers provide the calculator Layer in a temporary
418	Effect scope and clean up before settling. They do not create a ManagedRuntime.
419	Both plain paths reuse `calculateReport`; dispatch and output decoding have one
420	owner. The Effect interface remains caller-composed and creates no runtime.
421	These lifetime changes fulfil part of the accepted fresh interface work; they
422	do not establish the later calculator UI, transport limits or whole-task acceptance.
423	
424	## Native website RPC (T003 locally accepted)
425	
426	`@taxkit/api-rpc` owns all nine named calculator-service procedures over canonical
427	calculator request/result/query/metadata Schemas. Its native server mounts POST
428	`/rpc` with JSON; handlers delegate to the corresponding
429	named `PublicCalculatorService` operation.
430	The protocol lives in the caller's Layer scope; each named operation acquires and
431	releases its native generated client's receive loop. Expected
432	calculator failures project to fixed reasons, while version disagreement,
433	unavailable transport, invalid replies and a complete-response deadline remain
434	separate checked failures. Independent adapter defects remain defects.
435	
436	Native parser ingress checks procedure tags, bounded identities/batches/headers
437	and a 64-KiB UTF-8 input before dispatch. Native per-procedure and global defect
438	encoding use a fixed value. The client marks only the native exit reply decoder;
439	it does not classify every SchemaError as an invalid response. Installed Effect
440	4.0.0 source and actual wire tests qualify these hooks. RPC APIs remain unstable.
441	
442	The [package README](../../packages/api/rpc/README.md) owns its explicit exports
443	and current proof limits. The native API/Website candidates now consume it.
444	The saved Website pair check exercises actual built artifacts, repeated private
445	binding calls, an idle browser form, exact browser CORS and no-JavaScript POST.
446	The saved native RPC failure check also runs malformed envelopes, procedure
447	decoding, expected/version errors and an injected fatal operation in actual
448	Workers. A damaged valid-JSON reply crosses the real private binding and
449	restores a checked error in Chromium without replay. Fixed host log events are
450	required as positive controls. The native cancellation test runs the real
451	calculation/encoder before controlled twelve-second header/body delays. The
452	generated client must hit its ten-second deadline; Chromium must abort on the
453	deadline, editing and browser Back leaving the form. This establishes caller
454	cancellation, with no upstream Worker cancellation claim. Native local development
455	is separately qualified; T009 safe exported tracing remains in progress.
456	Public HTTP/OpenAPI keeps its existing contract and shared application operation.
457	
458	Calculator Schemas use narrow core/rule Schema entrypoints. Diagnostics and
459	report/input definitions have separate canonical modules; old entrypoints
460	re-export the same definitions. Browser transport imports therefore avoid live
461	engine/calculator/rule-pack modules. This changes export ownership, not tax
462	rules or retained report values. It does not change the SDK's deliberate local
463	calculation composition.
464	
465	## Export boundaries
466	
467	The SDK package should publish a dist-only export map. Workspace-local source
468	conditions are useful during early scaffolding, but they must not appear in the
469	publish manifest unless source files are also intentionally packed and
470	supported.
471	
472	Release packages express the two views separately: workspace `exports` may
473	retain `source`, while `publishConfig.exports` owns built `types` and `default`
474	targets and `files` limits the tarball. Because Bun resolves workspace and
475	catalogue dependency protocols during packing but does not apply
476	`publishConfig.exports`, the SDK-owned strict validator stages that declared
477	publication view and Bun-packs it again. Acceptance is based on the final
478	tarball manifest, clean installation and public-entrypoint imports. The
479	validator decodes the staged manifest once through a Schema that preserves
480	uninterpreted metadata, then encodes the declared publication view. Optional
481	dependency keys remain absent when originally absent; staged JSON key order is
482	not an artifact-byte guarantee. Each process has a scope, bounded stdout and
483	safe operational failures. A failed cleanup also fails validation.
484	
485	```json
486	{
487	  "exports": {
488	    ".": {
489	      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
490	      "default": "./dist/index.js"
491	    },
492	    "./effect": {
493	      "types": "./dist/effect.d.ts",
494	      "default": "./dist/effect.js"
495	    },
496	    "./au": {
497	      "types": "./dist/au.d.ts",
498	      "default": "./dist/au.js"
499	    },
500	    "./au/effect": {
501	      "types": "./dist/au-effect.d.ts",
502	      "default": "./dist/au-effect.js"
503	    },
504	    "./schemas": {
505	      "types": "./dist/schemas/index.d.ts",
506	      "default": "./dist/schemas/index.js"
507	    },
508	    "./testing": {
509	      "types": "./dist/testing/index.d.ts",
510	      "default": "./dist/testing/index.js"
511	    }
512	  }
513	}
514	```
515	
516	`.` should expose the plain, jurisdiction-neutral `TaxKit` facade. `./effect`
517	should expose the Effect-native `TaxKit` facade used by HTTP handlers.
518	Jurisdiction subpaths such as `./au` and `./au/effect` should expose local
519	typed modules, calculation descriptors and thin convenience clients. The current
520	plain root uses the default public calculator catalog, which includes the AU
521	rules through the calculator live Layer. The root does not directly import AU
522	descriptors; module selection limits client types rather than removing unselected
523	rules from that default catalog or proving a smaller bundle. `./schemas` must be
524	browser-safe and re-export calculator-owned `CalculatorRun*` schemas and
525	`CalculatorServiceError` without duplicating them. `./testing` may expose
526	test-only descriptors and helpers for consumers validating type behaviour.
527	
528	## Fumadocs site
529	
530	The current local documentation reader lives under:
531	
532	```txt
533	apps/web
534	```
535	
536	Reusable docs content and Fumadocs integration live under:
537	
538	```txt
539	packages/docs-content
540	packages/docs-fumadocs
541	```
542	
543	The docs app should document:
544	
545	- rule package architecture
546	- supported Australian tax years
547	- calculator inputs and outputs
548	- API reference
549	- SDK usage
550	- contribution guide for official rule tables and golden tests
551	
552	
553	The private catalogue procedure delegates to
554	`PublicCalculatorService.listCalculators` with the canonical `MetadataQuery`
555	and `CalculatorCatalogResponse`. It carries no calculation facts. Native
556	envelope admission derives its allowed tags from the owning nine-procedure group;
557	each operation retains the same checked version, safe defect handling, body
558	limits, whole-response deadline, native client scope and fetch policy. The
559	private reply decoder marks only the group's owning native exit Schemas; an
560	unrelated adapter Schema error remains a defect. Public HTTP/OpenAPI and SDK
561	interfaces do not change. The Website consumes this catalogue through its existing server application.
562	
563	The native body reader and RPC byte admission share
564	`CalculatorRequestBodyLimit` from `@taxkit/api-http/request-boundary`: 64 KiB.
565	The RPC export preserves its original four-symbol compatibility alias.
566	The API applies it to public HTTP and native RPC POST, and the Website applies
567	it before decoding any supported standard HTML calculator form. At exactly
568	the limit, valid JSON still reaches the same named calculation operation;
569	exceeding it releases the source before its remaining tail is consumed.
570	The retained standalone HTTP server mounts the same admission middleware.
571	Oversized/stalled bodies return fixed Schema-owned 413/408 JSON guidance; native
572	Website forms select fixed HTML guidance and a link back to the calculators.
573	The five-second total reader budget also rejects late synchronous completion.
574	Custom route/RPC-only hosts must supply request admission at their composition.
575	The native rate policy is described below; whole T004 qualification remains active.
576	
577	The private RPC client owns one ten-second complete-response deadline and a
578	2 MiB byte cap for all nine closed JSON replies. Its concrete native HTTP adapter
579	scopes each request through status validation and bounded stream reading before
580	reusing native Response/Protocol/exit codecs. HTTP 408, 413 and 429 have distinct
581	checked errors with fixed codes, literal safe messages and manual retry guidance;
582	no rejected body or raw HTTP cause reaches the page. Both calculator containers
583	share safe guidance for current and restored checked failures without replay.
584	The public SDK and standalone HTTP server retain their separate contracts.
585	
586	## Shared calculation work limits
587	
588	The [calculator-owned policy](../../packages/calculators/README.md#shared-calculation-work-limits)
589	supplies one eight-calculation pool and five-second operation budget to the native HTTP/RPC
590	instance and one per standalone HTTP router. Calculation errors use separately
591	declared HTTP 503/504 envelopes; existing request failures keep 400 and metadata
592	methods declare checked 504 timeouts without using calculation places. RPC revision 3 preserves the canonical fixed capacity and
593	timeout errors. Website forms request manual retry. SDK Schemas re-export these
594	errors, while local SDK execution keeps its caller-owned lifetime and tax results.
595	The owning package records cleanup and CPU proof limits. The native rate policy
596	and qualified MCP operations are described below; T006 retains the observed
597	modern five-second remote cleanup limit.
598	
599	
600	The [complete RPC contract](../../packages/api/rpc/README.md#complete-named-operation-contract)
601	keeps the nine application methods closed and named. The existing group is the
602	single source for native tag admission and owned reply-decoder identities.
603	Its private operation transformation owns native receive-loop cleanup and safe
604	transport policy over an already constructed Effect. It is not a client callback
605	escape. Public HTTP/OpenAPI and local SDK operations keep their existing owners.
606	
607	
608	SDK descriptor output narrowing checks `Schema.toType(outputSchema)` because
609	the calculator service already returns a domain report. Applying the transport
610	decoder again fails once trace fields are Options. HTTP/RPC representations
611	still encode/decode through their owning codecs. The packed consumer compares
612	22 saved metadata responses and the original trace/ledger bytes while its
613	declarations expose the new Core Option types and checked constructor inputs.
614	
615	
616	Calculator-owned context, help and filter fields use `Option<Option<A>>` in
617	checked TypeScript values: `None` means a missing key, `Some(None)` means a
618	present undefined key, and `Some(Some(value))` means a present value. Owning
619	constructors default omitted keys to `None`. JSON and HTTP query fields retain
620	their ordinary optional representation. Flatten the two absent forms only where
621	they mean the same thing; do not invent a jurisdiction or tax year.
622	
623	SDK constructor-input aliases retain the selected descriptor facts relation.
624	The SDK checks context/help through their owning Schemas and leaves facts to
625	the selected calculator decoder. HTTP/RPC use canonical Types internally and
626	representation codecs at serialisation. Their existing wire/OpenAPI fields and
627	values remain the compatibility contract.
628	
629	
630	Core calculation errors now retain diagnostic-key identity through nested
631	Options. Current rule errors omit diagnostics; historical opaque/null values
632	remain codec values and are not safe telemetry. Catalogue entries use their
633	checked selected continuation without the unused generic `program` field.
634	The fresh package declarations change deliberately; retained HTTP/RPC, report,
635	metadata and table/source values stay fixed. The active plan and domain-contract
636	receipt own qualification; native rate admission below still needs whole-slice
637	qualification before T004 can close.
638	
639	
640	## Native calculation rate admission
641	
642	The [calculator rate owner](../../packages/calculators/README.md#native-calculation-rate-admission) defines canonical errors and a redacted IP key. The [native API](../../apps/api/README.md#native-calculation-rate-admission) composes admission once below bounded work, so HTTP/RPC/private Website calls share an allowance and each batch member takes one unit. Metadata remains independent. HTTP uses 429 with `Retry-After: 60` or fixed 503 guidance; RPC revision 4 preserves the same errors. The standalone Bun host and local engine/SDK keep their existing behaviour. Packed declarations must expose the expanded checked error union without adding private host identity capabilities to the published RPC exports.
643	
644	### Native documentation RPC
645	
646	The same API POST endpoint mounts five documentation procedures through
647	`TaxKitPublicRpcGroup`, composed with the unchanged nine-procedure calculator
648	group. Documentation has its own `DocsRpcClient` and revision 2; calculator
649	revision 4 and its required client methods are preserved. The server requires
650	the calculator, content lookup and discovery services, supplied once at API
651	composition. The content handlers
652	reuse the generated accepted catalogue and canonical values; they run no
653	calculation and take no calculator allowance.
654	
655	Both private client groups share the native scoped 2 MiB response reader, then
656	project its private marker into their own errors. Documentation calls have a
657	ten-second complete-response deadline, caller cancellation, credential/redirect
658	and tracing policy, checked version skew and decoder-only invalid-reply marker.
659	Their fixed page/search/discovery errors and path bounds belong to `@taxkit/content`.
660	Page/search failures and public page paths are shared with HTTP. Native fatal defects retain the existing safe global
661	literal; procedure defects use the declared documentation literal. Defects stay
662	defects. The Website now supplies that client over its private binding and
663	uses browser-safe compiled MDX presentation. Its native GET loader transports
664	only a bounded public page identity; original SSR pathnames own page selection.
665	There is no authored-source fallback in the Website. Its `/search` form uses
666	the same named `searchDocs` operation, term and result limits. Browser native
667	GET carries an ASCII URI component header; original SSR words cannot be
668	overridden by that header. Empty words skip the operation. The private app
669	connection preserves the four public HTTP content routes. The fifth named
670	documentation call changes the private documentation revision. It returns a
671	closed discovery document derived from accepted content and the API application's
672	checked, lazy cached stage settings; the client checks its returned file path
673	against the requested one. Shared origin validation has separate API/Website
674	identities. The Website serves the four conventional files without reading MDX
675	source or constructing another runtime.
676	
677	
678	The Website's same-page Markdown HTTP policy delegates to the existing named
679	`getMarkdown` client operation. Explicit Website `.md` links and weighted
680	Accept selection add no public API endpoint, private RPC operation or revision.
681	The checked original page identity selects the accepted processed body. Native
682	HTTP composition keeps the same caller scope, deadline and safe failures;
683	[frontend architecture](frontend.md#replacement-website-markdown) owns the
684	Website's representation and response-header policy.
685	
686	
687	## Native remote MCP candidate
688	
689	The native API adds the app-owned `/mcp` adapter using installed Effect
690	`McpServer`, `Tool` and `Toolkit`. Its six named tools use canonical calculator
691	and accepted-content Schemas, delegating to the same captured services as
692	HTTP/RPC. Successful reports and processed Markdown are existing domain values;
693	fixed transport failures contain no submitted facts or underlying causes.
694	The safe reporter remains the single application error owner.
695	
696	Modern `2026-07-28` is composed in the native Worker; older `2025-11-25`
697	is composed in one app-owned, fixed-name Durable Object per stage. The SDK owns
698	its generated class, binding and runtime composition. Native Effect owns message
699	parsing, session IDs, version/header agreement and notification matching. The
700	plain/in-process composition remains modern-only.
701	
702	The API owns original connection identity, streamed POST admission and total
703	reply bounds. Its private object forwarding replaces a caller-supplied key
704	header with the checked original capability, separately from JSON. Native rate
705	admission is common to both adapters and HTTP/RPC, subject to the provider's
706	location and approximation contract. Each application isolate has its own
707	captured eight-place calculation pool and five-second work budget; no global
708	pool is claimed.
709	
710	Older host lifetime is ten minutes from first admission, with 32 initialisation
711	attempts and 32 concurrent requests without a queue. Expiry closes the entire
712	native protocol scope, releasing its in-memory sessions and work. The native
713	alarm owns unattended expiry; an incoming time check also refuses old IDs.
714	Clients need a fresh handshake after 404, including after a runtime eviction;
715	no conversation resumption is promised. The native adapter itself rejects
716	initialise carrying an existing ID before registration, preserving existing
717	conversations and their exhausted allocation allowance. Native alarm bookkeeping
718	is the only storage operation; neither client metadata nor figures are persisted.
719	
720	Host registration excludes the first caller's request, rate key and stop signal.
721	Replies retain native JSON/SSE framing, bounded to 2 MiB and ten seconds. No
722	subscription, GET stream, termination or resumption contract is added. Older
723	network cancellation is conversation-scoped and immediately releases actual
724	work. The modern real-network pre-response abort still relies on the existing
725	five-second work budget; earlier in-process cancellation does not prove prompt
726	remote cleanup. Public setup explains this limit rather than promising prompt
727	modern cancellation. The accepted [agent guide](../../packages/docs-content/content/api/agent-tools.mdx)
728	owns connection steps, the discovered tool names, input-first use, older expiry
729	and experimental browser support. The Website's `/agents` route derives its
730	remote MCP address from checked same-stage API settings and links that guide;
731	processed Markdown and documentation discovery reuse the accepted catalogue.
732	
733	The memory-only native source builder consumes computed SDK exports from the
734	actual app declaration, refusing provider/credential/network access. Tests must
735	load the generated native class and use actual clients and platform alarms,
736	rather than substitute bindings or handwritten frames. See the
737	[API owner](../../apps/api/README.md#native-remote-calculator-tools-candidate),
738	[session candidate record](../documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/2026-10-07-native-mcp-sessions.json)
739	and [browser owner](frontend.md#page-owned-browser-tools).
740	Current app-owned transport changes do not change a published package export or
741	the SDK lifetime contract.

10	# Testing and quality
11	
12	TaxKit quality depends on deterministic calculation tests, package boundary
13	tests, graph validation, trace snapshots, public contract tests and a working
14	Website/API. Detailed rule-package expectations live in
15	[Testing and validation](./testing-and-validation.md).
16	
17	## The checks
18	
19	| Command | What it shows |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| `bun run verification` | Before merging. Build, format, lint, workspace and Alchemy-root types, Effect diagnostics, unit tests, Chromium tests, both Knip graphs, documentation links/commands and portable paths. |
22	| `bun run test` | Unit tests in every workspace plus the root tool tests, including the actual-Oxlint rule fixtures. |
23	| `bun run test:browser` | Website and SDK tests in Chromium: Atom registry lifetime, calculator commands, loader cancellation and SDK browser imports. |
24	| `bun run test:native` | Builds the API and Website and runs them together in Miniflare: first HTML, docs pages, Markdown, discovery files, calculation with and without JavaScript, MCP and request limits. |
25	| `bun run release:check` | `verification` plus packed SDK, downstream consumer, API smoke, docs validation and Changeset status. Run it before a package release. |
26	
27	Focused checks are the owning workspace's `test`, `check-types` and
28	`test:browser` scripts. Rule and calculator changes need their golden and
29	boundary tests; HTTP contract changes need `bun run --filter=@taxkit/api-http test`
30	and an updated OpenAPI snapshot.
31	
32	## What each kind of change needs
33	
34	- **Tax rules, facts and calculators**: the rule package's golden scenarios,
35	  threshold/date-boundary tests and calculator catalogue tests. A wrong answer
36	  is the most serious failure TaxKit can have.
37	- **Public package contracts**: type tests, the OpenAPI snapshot, a Changeset,
38	  and the [packed consumer check](../runbooks/packed-consumer-proof.md) for SDK
39	  exports or dependencies.
40	- **Website or API runtime, bindings or client lifetime**: focused unit and
41	  browser tests, then `bun run test:native`.
42	- **Infrastructure**: `bun run check-types` covers the Alchemy roots. A native
43	  plan (`bun run pr:plan pr-<number>` or `bun run production:plan`) shows the
44	  intended resource changes before a deployment.
45	- **Documentation**: `bun run check:docs`; public MDX also needs
46	  `bun run docs:validate`.
47	
48	## Checks that stay separate
49	
50	Local checks do not show hosted behaviour. After a deployment, check the
51	deployed Website and API directly, as the [deployment runbook](../runbooks/deployment.md)
52	describes: page and API responses, browser CORS, calculation with and without
53	JavaScript, `www` redirects and Cloudflare cache hits.
54	
55	A green check also does not show that a package was published. Do not turn a
56	failing meaningful check into a pass by removing its assertion or raising a
57	timeout without understanding the failure.
58	
59	## Guardrails
60	
61	- Tests use deterministic Layers and `TestClock`; ordinary unit tests do not
62	  use the live network or wall-clock sleeps.
63	- Every expected error branch and every Schema boundary has a test.
64	- Browser and native tests check cancellation, cleanup and response limits,
65	  not only the successful path.
66	- Privacy tests check that logs, traces and analytics never contain salaries,
67	  supplied facts, results or calculation traces.
68	
69	## Related docs

73	- [Frontend](./frontend.md)
74	- [Deployment](./deployment.md)

The calculator should be small and declarative. Rule layers derive the facts. Scenario layers provide the accepted inputs.

Reusable catalogue entries couple one input Schema with its typed `calculate`
continuation. They do not expose an additional erased `program` Effect. The
rule package owns the actual typed calculator program and rule-pack Layer;
metadata and retained output values are unchanged.

## Running A Calculator

```ts
const calculation = CalculateTakeHomePay.pipe(
  Effect.provide(AuTakeHomePay2025_26_Live),
  Effect.provide(TakeHomeScenarioLiveFromInput(input))
);
```

Here `input` is the checked rule-owned scenario Type. The application runner
executes this lazy program; awaiting an Effect does not execute it. The compiler
shows unresolved requirements if a rule pack or scenario is missing.

## Calculator Domains

The retained calculator programs are goal-specific:

```txt
CalculateTakeHomePay
CalculatePayWithholdings
CalculateAnnualTax
```

Avoid one large `calculate()` function with mode switches for PAYG, annual tax, FBT, super, mortgage and deductions.

## Scenario Layers

Scenario layers decode user input through Effect Schema, then provide accepted input facts.

```txt
User input
  -> schema decode
  -> scenario dates
  -> accepted fact layer
  -> calculator
```

Scenario construction must fail if required boundary values are invalid. It should not silently coerce ambiguous tax-significant values.

Expected failures stay in the typed Effect error channel. Schema decode errors
should be mapped to schema-backed public errors at the service boundary, and
domain failures such as `CalculationError` should propagate as failures. Do not
use `Effect.die` for recoverable calculator, schema or domain errors.

Core `CalculationError.cause` represents missing, present undefined and present
diagnostic values with nested Options and a missing-key constructor default.
Its codec retains historical null/opaque diagnostics as values. The current
rule producers omit diagnostics; this migration does not sanitise legacy
diagnostic content or make it safe for telemetry. Public representations retain
their existing codec.

A calculator is an Effect program that requires facts and returns a report. It does not import global rule registries and it does not mutate shared state.

Calculator ids and context values are canonical boundary values. Shared scalar
brands such as `CalculatorId`, `Jurisdiction` and `TaxYear` live in

# Australian Pay Rules

Implemented rule package for Australian take-home pay and PAYG withholding.

## Scope

`@taxkit/rules-au-pay` owns gross pay, taxable pay, PAYG withholding,
withholdings ledger, net pay, salary-sacrifice pay effects, Schedule 1
parameters, descriptors, rule packs, calculator program and golden tests.

`TakeHomePayReport.rulePackVersion` is the exact literal
`rules-au-pay/1.0.0`. It versions this package's ruleset independently from the
package manifest version so callers can identify the pay rules used without
runtime manifest reads.

## Guardrails

- Reuse canonical schemas, facts, parameter services, rule IDs and component
  IDs from this package and `@taxkit/core`.
- Use Effect `Layer`s for rule derivations and parameter services.
- Use Effect `Array`, `HashMap`, `HashSet`, `Match`, `Context`, `Layer`,
  `Schema`, `Data`, `Record`, `Result` and `Exit` where they fit.
- Do not mirror canonical IDs or fact shapes as local `string` or DTO fields.
- Keep official Schedule 1 parameters separate from algorithms.
- Schedule 1 checks inclusive weekly row bounds and multipliers from zero to
  one. Each supported scale starts at zero, covers adjacent cents and has only
  its final bound open. The saved and decoded table forms share the same
  coverage check. Signed dollar coefficients remain valid, including the
  retained negative coefficient; both authored years stay unchanged.
- Derived money and ledger amounts use the core fallible constructors. An
  unsupported amount returns a safe `CalculationError` through the Effect
  error channel. `buildPayWithholdingsLedger` now returns an Effect; callers
  yield its result. Retained Schedule 1 values and known pay results are unchanged.

## Commands

```sh
bun run --filter=@taxkit/rules-au-pay check-types
bun run --filter=@taxkit/rules-au-pay test
```

## Packaging

The build removes `dist` before compiling. Workspace exports retain `source`
conditions, while `publishConfig.exports` and `files` define a dist-only
tarball validated by the SDK-owned strict downstream gate.

The Fumadocs generated-source boundary follows the same rule.
`@taxkit/docs-fumadocs/service` exposes only named `getPage` and `listPages`
Effects over schema-decoded generic page values. Its live Layer accepts one
